# `additional-properties-allowed`

additionalProperties allowed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `additional-properties-allowed` (both directions), `additional-properties-allowed-in-request`, `additional-properties-allowed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`additionalProperties` became `true` or a wider schema.

## Why this default

In requests: more requests are valid. In responses: clients may receive fields they were not written to handle.

## Example

From test case [`additional-properties-allowed`](../../test/cases/additional-properties-allowed/): additionalProperties false was removed from a response.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-       additionalProperties: false
```

Findings:

- `additional-properties-allowed-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  additional-properties-allowed: warn
```

## How to fix

Document that clients must ignore unknown fields.
